info.title: Sphericon Service API
info.description: The Staff surface a service calls with a Service credential (ADR 0026). It is served only by the internal listener, never on the public port.

get.description:
The changes of Tracking domain hosts since an opaque cursor, in the order they were
made: a host entering `dns_verified` or `serving`, moving between them, or leaving
them, which is reported as `removed` and never as silence. A caller that applies each
entry in order (provision on `dns_verified` and `serving`, tear down on `removed`)
mirrors the Instance's verified hosts, and a caller that starts from an empty cursor
rebuilds the whole set. Delivery is at-least-once: replaying a cursor returns the same
entries, so applying one twice must change nothing.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of a page the caller has saved; empty starts from the beginning

the open period, Usage snapshots for a closed one. Never a recount on read.

get.description:
The Workspaces created or changed since an opaque cursor, each with all of its
owners, in a stable order by change position. A change is a new Workspace, an owner
added, removed or transferred, or an owner's email or verification changing.
Delivery is at-least-once: replaying a cursor returns the same entries, and an
empty cursor starts from the beginning.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of a page the caller has saved; empty starts from the beginning

UsagePeriodQuery.name: period
UsagePeriodQuery.description: The Usage period as YYYY-MM (UTC); the current one when absent

EntityId.description:
A primary key, written as a decimal string so JavaScript never rounds it. The format
makes the Go servers parse it into an int64: a malformed id is refused as a 400 before
a handler runs. The pattern says the same in the contract, so a client (or a fuzzer) can
tell a malformed id from a valid one without trying it. Eighteen digits is the most a key
reaches, so every id the schema admits fits an int64.

GoneProblem.description: RFC 7807 gone response: the resource existed but is no longer available (an expired link)

changed.description: False when no such hold was set and nothing changed, so a retry is visibly harmless

HoldClearResult.description: The outcome of clearing a hold

reasonCode.description: A machine code for the reason: lowercase letters, digits and underscores

message.description: The message shown to the Workspace Owner, as given

actionUrl.description:
Where the Workspace's Owners and Admins can resolve the hold, shown as a link next to the message:
an absolute https URL. Omit it to give none; setting the hold again without it removes a stored one.

expiresAt.description: Required; in the future and no further than the configured maximum from now

HoldList.description: The active holds of a Workspace

key.description: The key the setter chose; unique per Workspace

reasonCode.description: A machine code for the reason

message.description: The message shown to the Workspace Owner, as given

actionUrl.description: Where the Workspace's Owners and Admins can resolve the hold; absent when none was given

expiresAt.description: When the hold stops freezing sending unless its setter renews it

setBy.description: The name of the Service credential that last set it

createdAt.description: When the hold was first set

updatedAt.description: When the hold was last set or renewed

HoldResource.description: A Staff hold: one reversible freeze of a Workspace's outbound sending (ADR 0009)

changed.description: False when the hold was already set exactly so and nothing changed, so a retry is visibly harmless

hold.description: The hold as it is stored now

HoldSetResult.description: The outcome of setting a hold

InUseProblem.description:
RFC 7807 conflict response for a removal refused because live work still uses the row
(ADR 0049): 409 with `usedBy` naming the users. Every refused removal of a Segment, Tag,
Integration, Sending domain or Automation answers it.

code.description: Why the request was refused, when the client should act on it

type.description: A URI reference that identifies the problem type

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type

detail.description: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence

instance.description: A URI reference that identifies the specific occurrence

retryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; set on a 429 so a client that only sees the body can show the wait

debug.description: Why a 500 happened, sent only by a development server (`SPHERICON_ENV=development`)

usedBy.description: The live rows that use the one a removal was refused for, never empty

InUseProblemDetails.description: The body of a refused removal (ADR 0049): ProblemDetails plus the rows that use it

PaymentRequiredProblem.description: RFC 7807 payment required response: the feature needs an Enterprise license

PreconditionRequiredProblem.description:
RFC 7807 precondition required response: the request needs something it did not carry
(a verification link opened outside its Sign-up browser needs a password, ADR 0030)

ProblemCode.description: A machine-readable reason a client branches on, beyond the HTTP status

error.description: The error that failed the request, or the panic value

stack.description: The goroutine stack of a panic; absent for an error a handler returned

requestId.description: The request id the server log carries for this request

method.description: The HTTP method of the failed request

path.description: The path of the failed request

ProblemDebug.description:
What a development server adds to a 500 so the page can show the fault; a production
Instance never sends it

type.description: A URI reference that identifies the problem type

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type

detail.description: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence

instance.description: A URI reference that identifies the specific occurrence

retryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; set on a 429 so a client that only sees the body can show the wait

debug.description: Why a 500 happened, sent only by a development server (`SPHERICON_ENV=development`)

name.description: The service's name, as recorded in the Audit log

expiresAt.description: When the credential stops working; absent when it never expires

ServiceIdentityResource.description: What a Service credential is: its name, its scopes and its expiry

ServiceScope.description: A scope a Service credential may carry

workspaceId.description: The Workspace that held the host at this change

state.description:
What the host became; `removed` is the explicit report that it left the verified
states. Entries of one host arrive in the order they happened, so the last one read
is its current state.

ServiceTrackingHostChange.description: One change of a Tracking domain host

items.description: Changes after the requested cursor, in the order they were made

nextCursor.description:
Pass it back as the cursor to read what follows this page. It is the requested
cursor itself when the page is empty. Saving it is what advances the caller: the
core keeps no position of its own.

hasMore.description: Whether more entries follow this page right now

ServiceTrackingHostFeedPage.description: One page of the Tracking host feed

ServiceTrackingHostState.description: What a Tracking domain host did at one change

items.description: Workspaces created or changed after the requested cursor, in change order

nextCursor.description:
Pass it back as the cursor to read what follows this page. It is the requested
cursor itself when the page is empty. Saving it is what advances the caller: the
core keeps no position of its own.

hasMore.description: Whether more entries follow this page right now

ServiceWorkspaceFeedPage.description: One page of the Workspace feed

emailVerifiedAt.description: When the owner confirmed their email; absent while it is unverified

ServiceWorkspaceOwner.description: One owner of a Workspace in the feed

id.description: The Workspace id: its short opaque public address (ADR 0043)

discardedAt.description:
When the Workspace was deleted; absent while it is live or after a restore. Its
30-day window runs from here.

erasedAt.description:
When the erasure job removed the Workspace's data; absent until then. An erased
Workspace stays in the feed as a tombstone: its name is blank and it has no owners.

owners.description: Every owner of the Workspace as of this entry

ServiceWorkspaceResource.description: A Workspace with all of its owners, as the feed reports it

value.description: The value of the metric over the period

final.description:
True once the Usage period closed: the figure is a Usage snapshot and never changes.
False while it is Live usage.

computedAt.description: When the figure was last computed

UsageFigure.description: One metric's figure for a Workspace over a Usage period

kind.description: What kind of row it is

count.description:
How many rows the entry stands for; absent means one. An `enrollment` entry names the
Automation (id, name) and counts its Enrollments; a `message` entry names it and counts its
sent Outbound messages.

UsedBy.description:
A row that uses the one a removal was refused for: what a client shows to say what to
change first

UsedByKind.description:
What kind of row a refused removal names as a user of the row (ADR 0049). One value per kind
of live user a removal can find, so a client branches on it without parsing text.

WorkspaceId.description:
A Workspace id (ADR 0043): 8 random base62 characters, assigned once at creation and the
Workspace's one public address.

period.description: The Usage period: the calendar month in UTC, as YYYY-MM

WorkspaceUsageResource.description: The figures of one Workspace for one Usage period
